where πεδοî [on the ground] was written with the agreement of Eustathius p. 1839, 57, which I corrected from Ioannes Alex. τον. παραγγ. p. 30, 8: τὰ ἀπὸ βαρυτόνων βαρύνεται, ἔξω ἔξοι, πέδον πέδοι. “πέδοι δὲ βᾶσαι” Αἰσχύλος Προμηθεῖ δεσμώτη [words from barytones are barytone, except ἔξω [outside] ἔξοι, πέδον [ground] πέδοι [on the ground]. "But going on the ground" Aeschylus in Prometheus Bound]. The same is prescribed by the scholiast on Dionysius Thrax in Bekker's Anecdota p. 945, 2; on the other hand it is counted among the perispomena in Reg. prosod. 173.
